books.name: Joshua
gists: God commissions Joshua to lead Israel with strength and obedience.
Joshua's spies are hidden by Rahab, who secures her family's safety.
Israel crossed the Jordan on dry ground as God parted the waters.
Twelve stones from the Jordan are erected as a memorial to God's faithfulness.
Israel's new generation is circumcised, celebrates Passover, and meets the LORD.
Israel marched around Jericho, causing its walls to fall.
Achan's sin leads to Israel's defeat and his eventual destruction.
Joshua ambushes Ai, destroys the city, and renews the covenant.
The Gibeonites deceive Israel, leading to a treaty and servitude.
Joshua defeats five Amorite kings and conquers their cities.
Joshua defeats northern kings, destroys Hazor, and conquers enemy cities.
Israel defeated kings east and west of Jordan and divided the land.
Joshua allocates land to nine and a half tribes; Levites receive offerings instead.
Caleb claimed Hebron, and land was divided among the tribes.
Judah's territory is defined, including Caleb's conquest of Hebron.
Ephraim's inheritance is defined, but Canaanites remain in Gezer.
Manasseh's land is allotted; Zelophehad's daughters inherit alongside brothers.
Israelites gather at Shiloh; land divided among tribes by lot.
Canaan's land is divided among tribes by lot, including Dan's conquest.
Joshua designates six cities of refuge for unintentional killers.
Israel allotted forty-eight cities to the Levites as commanded by God.
The eastern tribes build an altar to affirm unity, restoring peace.
Joshua encourages Israel's leaders to obey God and avoid idolatry.
Joshua challenges Israel to serve God, then dies at 110.

anchors.text: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.

And if it seem evil unto you to serve the LORD, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.

books.name: Judges
gists: Judah leads in conquering Canaanites, but many tribes fail to fully comply.
Israel turns to idolatry, prompting oppression and a cycle of sin.
Israel sins, faces oppression, and is delivered by Othniel, Ehud, and Shamgar.
Deborah and Barak defeat Sisera, bringing peace to Israel.
Deborah and Barak praise God for Israel's victory and peace.
Gideon is called by God to deliver Israel from Midianite oppression.
Gideon reduces his army to 300, surprises, and defeats the Midianites.
Gideon defeats Midianite kings and declines kingship, leading Israel to peace.
Abimelech kills his brothers to become king, leading to destruction and his death.
Israel sins, faces oppression, and repents, prompting God's mercy.
Jephthah leads Gilead against Ammon and sacrifices his daughter.
Ephraim challenges Jephthah, leading to civil strife and Gilead's victory.
An angel announces Samson's birth to a barren woman in Zorah.
Samson seeks a Philistine wife, slays a lion, and poses a riddle.
Samson exacts revenge on the Philistines, killing many after personal losses.
Samson reveals his strength to Delilah, is betrayed, and blinded.
Micah establishes a private idol shrine and hires a Levite priest.
The tribe of Dan conquers Laish and establishes idolatry.
A Levite's concubine is abused and killed in Gibeah.
Israel seeks justice against Benjamin, resulting in a devastating civil war.
Israelites seek to preserve Benjamin by capturing wives at Shiloh’s festival.

anchors.text: In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.

books.name: Ruth
gists: Naomi returns to Bethlehem with loyal Ruth after losing her family.
Boaz protects and provides for Ruth during the harvest.
Ruth seeks Boaz's protection; he promises to redeem her.
Boaz marries Ruth, securing lineage and family legacy, and they bear Obed.

anchors.text: And Ruth said, Intreat me not to leave thee, or to return from following after thee: for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God:

books.name: 1 Samuel
gists: Hannah prays for a son, vows him to the LORD, and bears Samuel.
Hannah praises God; Eli’s corrupt sons face prophetic judgment.
God calls Samuel at night, revealing judgment against Eli's house.
Israel suffers defeat to the Philistines; the Ark is captured.
The Philistines suffer plagues after capturing the ark and return it.
The Philistines return the ark, but God strikes down curious onlookers.
Samuel leads Israel to repent and defeats the Philistines.
Israel demands a king despite Samuel's warnings about oppressive rule.
Saul seeks lost donkeys and meets Samuel, who anoints him king.
Samuel anoints Saul, who is chosen king by Israel.
Saul defeats the Ammonites, solidifying his kingship at Gilgal.
Samuel warns against rejecting God and emphasizes obedience for blessing.
Saul's impatience leads to his rejection as king amid Philistine threats.
Jonathan and his armor-bearer defeat the Philistines, despite Saul’s foolish oath.
Saul disobeys God by sparing Amalek's king and livestock, leading to rejection.
Samuel anoints David as king, chosen for his heart over appearances.
David defeats Goliath, leading Israel to victory over the Philistines.
Jonathan befriends David, but Saul's jealousy leads to attempts on David's life.
Saul pursues David, but Jonathan helps David escape multiple times.
David and Jonathan establish a secret signal amid Saul's growing anger.
David seeks help at Nob and feigns madness in Gath.
David seeks refuge and gathers followers while Saul kills Nob's priests.
David defeats the Philistines, escapes Saul's plot, and finds strength in Jonathan.
David spares Saul's life, revealing his mercy in the cave.
Samuel dies; Abigail saves David from vengeance; Nabal dies; David marries Abigail.
David spares Saul in his camp, demonstrating respect for God's anointed.
David seeks refuge with Achish, deceiving him about his raids.
Saul consults a medium, learns of his impending doom, and feels distressed.
David is dismissed by the Philistines before the battle at Jezreel.
David rescues captured wives and recovers spoils from the Amalekites.
Saul and his sons die in battle against the Philistines.

anchors.text: And Samuel said, Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.

But the LORD said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the LORD seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.
And all this assembly shall know that the LORD saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the LORD’s, and he will give you into our hands.

books.name: 2 Samuel
gists: David mourns Saul and Jonathan’s deaths, condemning the man who claimed to kill Saul.
David is anointed king over Judah; conflict arises with Ishbosheth's reign.
David gains power as Abner seeks alliance; Joab kills Abner, leading to mourning.
Ishbosheth is murdered; David executes the assassins and honors justice.
David is anointed king, captures Jerusalem, and defeats the Philistines.
David brings the ark to Jerusalem, celebrating amid Michal's disdain.
God promises David an everlasting dynasty instead of a temple.
David expanded his kingdom by defeating enemies and securing tribute.
David shows kindness to Mephibosheth, restoring his land and welcoming him.
David defeats Ammon and their allies after humiliation of his servants.
David's adultery with Bathsheba leads to Uriah's death to hide the sin.
Nathan confronts David; he repents, but their child dies.
Amnon assaults Tamar; Absalom kills Amnon and flees.
David allows Absalom's return after a wise woman's appeal.
Absalom rises to power, and David flees Jerusalem with supporters.
David hears false claims about Mephibosheth and faces Shimei's curses.
Hushai advises Absalom, enabling David's escape; Ahithophel commits suicide.
David mourns Absalom after a battle that claims many lives.
David mourns Absalom; Joab urges him to honor loyal supporters.
Sheba's rebellion is quelled by a wise woman's negotiation.
David resolves a famine by atoning for Saul's wrongs against the Gibeonites.
David praises the LORD for rescue, strength, and divine justice.
David's last words praise God's covenant and honor mighty warriors.
David conducts a census, confesses sin, and faces divine punishment.

anchors.text: And thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.
And he said, The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer;

books.name: 1 Kings
gists: David anoints Solomon as king, rejecting Adonijah's claim.
David instructs Solomon, who then consolidates his kingdom by eliminating rivals.
Solomon received wisdom from God to wisely judge disputed parenthood.
Solomon's wisdom and administration lead to a prosperous and famous kingdom.
Hiram agrees to supply materials for Solomon's temple in exchange for provisions.
Solomon builds the temple, promising God's presence if he obeys.
Solomon completed his palace and commissioned various decorative temple items.
Solomon dedicates the temple, prays for God's presence and forgiveness.
God promises Solomon's throne in exchange for obedience; he completes the temple.
The queen of Sheba visits Solomon, impressed by his wisdom and wealth.
Solomon's idolatry led to divine judgment and kingdom division.
Rehoboam's harsh rule leads to Israel's revolt and Jeroboam's idolatrous reign.
A prophet disobeys God, leading to his death by a lion.
Jeroboam's son dies, and judgment against his house is pronounced.
Abijam and Asa reign in Judah, with Asa promoting reforms and victories.
Baasha's house is condemned; Elah is assassinated, and Omri reigns wickedly.
Elijah proclaims drought, lives by a brook, sustains a widow, revives her son.
Elijah proves the LORD's power over Baal on Mount Carmel.
Elijah flees, is fed by an angel, and encounters God at Horeb.
Ahab defeats Benhadad but is rebuked for sparing him.
Ahab covets Naboth's vineyard, leading to Naboth's death and God's judgment.
Ahab seeks Ramoth-gilead, is defeated, and dies in battle.

anchors.text: But will God indeed dwell on the earth? behold, the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this house that I have builded?
And Elijah came unto all the people, and said, How long halt ye between two opinions? if the LORD be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word.
And after the earthquake a fire; but the LORD was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.

books.name: 2 Kings
gists: Ahaziah seeks Baalzebub; Elijah declares his death and judges captains.
Elijah is taken to heaven, and Elisha inherits his prophetic authority.
Israel, Judah, and Edom unite; Elisha foretells victory over Moab.
Elisha performs miracles, demonstrating God’s power and provision during need.
Naaman is healed of leprosy by Elisha after washing in the Jordan.
Elisha aids prophets, recovers an axe head, and captures the Syrian army.
Elisha predicts food abundance; four lepers discover an abandoned Syrian camp.
Elisha predicts a famine, Hazael kills Benhadad, and Jehoram rules Judah.
Jehu is anointed king, kills Joram, Ahaziah, and Jezebel.
Jehu eliminates Ahab’s lineage and Baal worship, but retains idol worship.
Athaliah is overthrown; Joash is crowned king, restoring true worship.
Jehoash repairs the temple but is ultimately killed by his servants.
Jehoahaz and Joash defeat Syria, aided by Elisha's prophecy.
Amaziah reigns, defeats Edom, challenges Israel, faces defeat, and is killed.
Azariah reigns righteously but becomes leprous; Israel faces turmoil and Assyria's advance.
Ahaz forsook God, practiced idolatry, and sought Assyrian aid.
Israel falls to Assyria due to idolatry and rebellion.
Hezekiah reforms Judah, pays tribute to Assyria, and faces siege.
Hezekiah prays; God protects Jerusalem, defeating Assyria and Sennacherib.
Hezekiah recovers from illness after prayer, receiving a divine extension of life.
Manasseh's idolatry led to judgment; Amon ruled briefly before death.
Josiah discovers the law, repents, and receives a prophetic message.
Josiah renews the covenant, destroys idolatry, and dies; Judah faces judgment.
Judah faced punishment, Jehoiakim died, and Jehoiachin was captured by Babylon.
Jerusalem falls to Babylon; its temple is destroyed and people exiled.

anchors.text: And he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.

books.name: 1 Chronicles
gists: Genealogies from Adam to Abraham, including Esau's descendants and Edom's kings.
Judah's genealogy is traced, highlighting David and Caleb's lineage.
David's sons and their genealogy, leading to Zerubbabel, are detailed.
Genealogies of Judah and Simeon; Jabez's prayer leads to blessing.
Reuben's birthright was lost; genealogies of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh follow.
Levi's genealogy, priestly duties, and cities for Levites are detailed.
Genealogies and warriors of Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, and Asher.
Chapter 8 traces Benjamin's genealogy and notable descendants, including Saul.
Exiled Israelites settled in Jerusalem, with outlined genealogies and temple duties.
Saul and his sons die in battle; his body is recovered for burial.
David is anointed king, captures Jerusalem, and gains loyal warriors.
David unites loyal warriors and is proclaimed king in Hebron.
David attempts to bring the ark, but Uzza is struck down.
David builds his house with Hiram's help and defeats the Philistines.
David organizes the joyful transport of the ark to Jerusalem.
David brings the ark, offers thanks, and establishes perpetual worship.
God promises to establish David's kingdom and lineage forever.
David expands his kingdom through victories and dedicates spoils to God.
David's messengers are humiliated; Joab defeats Ammonites and Syrians, restoring peace.
David captures Rabbah; Israel fights and defeats Philistine giants.
David's census incurs God's wrath, leading to a devastating plague.
David prepares for the temple's construction and charges Solomon to lead.
David organizes the Levites for temple service and worship.
David organized priestly duties into twenty-four divisions by casting lots.
David organizes 288 musicians into 24 groups for worship.
Temple porters and gatekeepers manage treasures and responsibilities.
Israel's military organized into monthly divisions under various captains.
David charges Solomon to lead and build the temple with obedience.
David prepares for the Temple, blesses God, and Solomon is anointed king.

anchors.text: Seek the LORD and his strength, seek his face continually.

Thine, O LORD, is the greatness, and the power, and the glory, and the victory, and the majesty: for all that is in the heaven and in the earth is thine; thine is the kingdom, O LORD, and thou art exalted as head above all.

books.name: 2 Chronicles
gists: Solomon seeks God, offers sacrifices, and receives wisdom and riches.
Solomon enlists Tyrian craftsmen and foreign workers to build the temple.
Solomon builds and adorns the temple on Mount Moriah.
Solomon made temple furnishings and a large brass altar.
Solomon dedicates the temple and brings the Ark into the Most Holy Place.
Solomon dedicates the temple, praying for God's presence and mercy.
Fire consumes sacrifices; Solomon's dedication leads to God's promise and warning.
Solomon completed the temple, built cities, and established trade.
The queen of Sheba visits Solomon, impressed by his wisdom and wealth.
Rehoboam rejects wise counsel, leading to Israel's rebellion against David's house.
Rehoboam fortifies Judah, obeys God, and strengthens his kingdom.
Rehoboam's sin leads to Egypt's invasion and subservience.
Abijah defeats Jeroboam, affirming God's covenant and gaining strength in Judah.
Asa reforms Judah, defeats Zerah the Ethiopian, and secures victory.
Asa renews devotion to God, removes idols, and promotes peace.
Asa trusts Syria, is rebuked, and suffers illness leading to his death.
Jehoshaphat strengthens Judah, removes idolatry, and promotes law teaching.
Jehoshaphat allies with Ahab, leading to Ahab's defeat and death.
Jehoshaphat is rebuked for alliances, restores justice, and appoints judges.
Jehoshaphat seeks God's help, and enemies destroy themselves, leading to victory.
Jehoram reigns wickedly, provoking revolts and facing judgment and invasion.
Ahaziah reigns briefly, is slain by Jehu, while Joash is hidden.
Jehoiada crowns the king's son and eliminates Athaliah, restoring temple worship.
Joash forsakes God after Jehoiada's death, leading to his downfall.
Amaziah defeats Edom, turns to their gods, is defeated by Joash.
Uzziah's pride leads to leprosy and isolation; Jotham governs.
Jotham reigned righteously, fortified cities, and defeated the Ammonites.
Ahaz's wicked reign leads to Judah's defeat and idolatry.
Hezekiah cleanses the temple, restores worship, and offers sin sacrifices.
Hezekiah led a unified Passover celebration, restoring worship and joy.
Hezekiah restores worship, purges idolatry, and organizes offerings and provisions.
Sennacherib besieges Jerusalem, but God destroys the Assyrian army.
Manasseh repented after captivity, but Amon reverted to evil.
Josiah seeks God, cleanses idolatry, repairs the temple, and renews covenant.
Josiah holds an unprecedented Passover, is mortally wounded, and mourned by Judah.
Jerusalem falls to Babylon, leading to exile and later restoration decree by Cyrus.

anchors.text: If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.

For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. Herein thou hast done foolishly: therefore from henceforth thou shalt have wars.

And he said, Hearken ye, all Judah, and ye inhabitants of Jerusalem, and thou king Jehoshaphat, Thus saith the LORD unto you, Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s.

books.name: Ezra
gists: Cyrus orders the rebuilding of Jerusalem's temple, fulfilling prophecy.
42,360 Israelites return from Babylon, with some excluded due to lineage issues.
Israelites rebuilt the altar, laid the temple foundation, and celebrated joyfully.
Opponents impede temple rebuilding, halting work until Darius's reign.
Prophets encourage temple rebuilding, affirmed by elders amid an inquiry.
Darius confirms the decree, the temple is completed, and Passover is celebrated.
Ezra secures royal permission to lead Israelites back to Jerusalem.
Ezra leads the returnees, ensures temple service, and journeys safely to Jerusalem.
Ezra mourns Israel's intermarriage, prays for repentance and separation.
Ezra leads Israel in confessing sin and separating from foreign wives.

anchors.text: For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.

books.name: Nehemiah
gists: Nehemiah mourns Jerusalem’s suffering and prays for God's mercy.
Nehemiah secures royal favor to rebuild Jerusalem's walls and inspires leaders.
Priests and citizens unite to repair Jerusalem's walls and gates.
Enemies mock rebuilding efforts, but Nehemiah leads prayerful vigilance and perseverance.
Nehemiah addresses debt oppression, urging nobles to restore property and act justly.
Nehemiah overcomes opposition and completes the wall in 52 days.
Nehemiah registers returned exiles and appoints gatekeepers in Jerusalem.
Ezra read the Law, prompting worship, joy, and celebration of booths.
Israelites confess sins and renew covenant in acknowledgment of God's mercy.
Leaders covenanted to obey God's law and support the temple.
Leaders and people were assigned to inhabit and serve Jerusalem.
Nehemiah details priestly genealogies and the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
Nehemiah restores temple practices and enforces covenant faithfulness.

anchors.text: Then he said unto them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our LORD: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the LORD is your strength.

books.name: Esther
gists: King Ahasuerus removes Queen Vashti for refusing to appear at his feast.
Esther becomes queen after gaining Ahasuerus's favor and Mordecai saves the king.
Haman plots to destroy the Jews after Mordecai refuses to bow.
Esther resolves to approach the king to save her people.
Esther hosts a banquet, deferring her request, while Haman seethes at Mordecai.
The king honors Mordecai, unaware of Haman's plotting against him.
Esther reveals Haman's plot, leading to his execution.
Esther secures Jewish protection and joy after Haman's decree is revoked.
Jews defeated their enemies, feasted, and established Purim.
Mordecai gained authority and was respected for promoting Jewish welfare.

anchors.text: For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, then shall there enlargement and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place; but thou and thy father’s house shall be destroyed: and who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
